server.name: alion
server.title: Alion: company, startup and market intelligence
server.description: Live data on millions of companies worldwide: what they do, where they operate, the technologies they use, how they are funded and how fast they grow - read from their own sites, job boards and public registers - plus lookalike companies, verified job postings and hiring and pay statistics - and people open to offers: find them, read their open profiles and write to them in Alion messages.

tools.name: search_jobs
tools.title: Search job postings
tools.description: Search live or recently closed job postings read from employers' own ATS boards, career pages and partner feeds worldwide (strong in Europe, the Gulf, Central Asia and remote roles). Each row: employer, role family, seniority, work mode, locations (ISO codes; a remote role adds hiring_countries), the stated salary or a USD estimate with its method, required technologies, first seen and last verified dates, a trust verdict (ok, stale, ghost) and its Alion page url, where a candidate applies. Newest first, or by pay with sort=salary. Filters combine with AND; an unknown value returns a warning naming what was accepted. Agencies and job boards are left out unless include_agencies=true. Pass next_cursor back for the next page. For counts, pay percentiles or top employers call market_stats instead of paging. Costs 1 unit per call. Docs: https://alion.io/developers/docs

query.description: Free text over titles and descriptions, e.g. "python backend kubernetes": matched as a phrase first, else every word anywhere (filters_applied.query_match says which). An exact employer name returns its postings.

role.description: A role family ("Backend", "Data Science", "AI/ML") or a specialisation ("Data Engineer", "Product Manager"); a family covers its specialisations (alion://dictionaries/role-families). filters_applied.role shows the match.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (preferred) or country name. Matches the office country, the posting country, or the hiring country of a remote role when the posting states it (hiring_geo_confidence structured or explicit).

city.description: City in English, e.g. "Berlin", "Dubai", "Almaty"; "NYC", "Bay Area", "Munich/München" are understood. An unknown city is refused with suggestions.

work_mode.description: Where the work happens: on_site, hybrid or remote.

seniority.description: Seniority of the role: intern, junior, middle, senior, staff, lead or head.

employment_type.description: Kind of engagement: full_time, part_time, contractor, cofounder, freelance or internship.

salary_min_usd.description: Minimum annual pay in USD: a stated range whose top reaches it, or - when nothing is stated - an estimate whose midpoint does.

posted_since.description: Only postings first seen after this point: an ISO date ("2026-09-01") or a relative window ("24h", "7d", "2w").

company.description: Restrict to one employer: its Alion company id, domain ("stripe.com") or exact name.

industry.description: The industry of the posting or its employer, e.g. "Fintech", "Real Estate", "Gaming", "Healthcare" (the industries resource lists them). Every role at those employers; combine with role for one kind of job.

sector.description: A frontier-tech sector or a comma list: biotech, medtech, space, aerospace, semiconductors, energy, climate, defense, robotics, quantum, automotive, science - its trades at any employer and the technical roles of companies built on it (no sales or back office).

technology.description: A technology that must be among the requirements, e.g. "Go", "PostgreSQL", "React". A language also matches its frameworks.

visa_sponsorship.description: Only postings that state visa sponsorship.

visa_sponsor.description: Only employers in the official visa sponsor registers of the posting's country (UK licensed sponsors, US H-1B/PERM, Dutch IND, Canadian LMIA, Irish employment permits, Danish Fast-track, Australian labour agreements), on-site roles of direct employers in the Gulf states (where the employer arranges the work visa by law), or adverts that offer sponsorship; adverts ruling it out are excluded.

visa_salary.description: Only postings whose stated yearly pay reaches the posting country's work-permit salary floor (EU Blue Card in DE, FR, ES, PL, AT, CZ, FI, LU, SE, EE; Dutch highly skilled migrant; Irish Critical Skills; Danish Pay Limit; Singapore Employment Pass; Korean E-7). Postings without a stated salary are excluded.

include_agencies.description: Include postings by staffing and recruiting agencies and by intermediaries (job boards, talent marketplaces).

status.description: "closed" returns postings confirmed closed on the employer board (with closed_at), useful for time-to-fill and churn analysis.

detail.description: "compact" returns about a third of each row (who, what, where, pay, when, trust) - use it to scan many rows; "standard" adds requirements, locations, verification facts and a 280-character description snippet.

tools.name: resolve_company
tools.title: Resolve a company
tools.description: Find the company record behind a domain, a url or a name and learn whether it is alive: its Alion id, canonical domain, industry, size band, headquarters, ATS vendor, how many jobs are open, when the site and the job board were last verified, and coverage - ats_board when its own job board is read directly, partial when only feeds and career pages reach us (open-job counts are then a lower bound). Call this first whenever you only have a name or a domain, then pass the id to get_company or search_jobs. A domain match is exact (or on the registrable domain, e.g. jobs.acme.com -> acme.com); a name match reports its confidence (name_exact, name_prefix, name_partial, with _ambiguous when several records fit) and lists the candidates so you can pick. Costs 1 unit per call. Docs: https://alion.io/developers/docs

tools.name: search_companies
tools.title: Search companies
tools.description: Find companies in Alion's live graph (millions worldwide, one per web domain) by name or domain prefix, office country, size, industry or frontier sector, founding year, startup or not, funding stage, rounds since a date, minimum round, a named investor, a technology from its job postings, ATS vendor, hiring now, and growth (hiring_level A-C) or AI-adoption level. For market maps, competitor and prospect lists, deal flow and technology-adoption research. Each row: headquarters, founding year, startup verdict, newest round and total raised, open jobs and jobs added in 30 days, last verified date. Default order: most recent hiring; sort=recent_funding, open_jobs, score, newest or name. Agencies are left out unless include_agencies=true. Pass next_cursor back for the next page. Lookalikes: similar_companies; one company in depth: get_company. detail=compact costs the least, and connected assistants get a daily allowance of compact reads free. tools.name: market_stats
tools.title: Hiring and pay statistics
tools.description: Aggregate statistics for a slice of the job market in one call: how much X earns in Y, how many companies hire X, whether demand grows, who hires most, how fast such roles close. Takes the search_jobs filters plus window_days and returns: open postings and hiring companies; new postings in 30 days against the 30 before (trend_30d_pct); work-mode and seniority mix; salary p10-p90 in USD a year, stated and estimated apart, with the transparency rate; time to fill in days; the top 10 employers; and, among the 3000 newest postings, the top 15 technologies and the top countries. Every block has its sample size n; percentiles are null under 5 postings. Cached up to 6 hours; a block not computed in time is listed under partial with null figures (unknown, not zero) - repeat in a minute. Costs 2 units per call. Docs: https://alion.io/developers/docs

tools.name: send_message
tools.title: Write to a person
tools.description: Write to a person in their Alion messages. The first message is an offer: purpose, the job (title, pay, places, work mode), on whose behalf, why this person (a fact of their profile) and the text (30-2000 characters, in their language). Delivered only if it passes the person's filters and the rules, else returned at once, unseen, with a reason and a hint: role_mismatch, pay_below_floor, location_mismatch, not_personal, already_contacted (one company, one approach in 90 days), declined_recently, bulk_message, content_rules (no money, documents, outside contacts or AI instructions), link_not_allowed, company_not_verified, person_busy. Past the person's daily cap it waits in a queue up to 7 days. Delivered, it gives conversation_id; read answers with get_conversation or set_webhook. To continue, pass conversation_id and message (before an answer, one reminder after 7 days). New conversations a day: no account 2, a wallet 5, an account as on the site, a verified company 50. Docs: https://alion.io/developers/docs

tools.name: contact_company
tools.title: Write to a company
tools.description: Write to a company through Alion: purpose (sales, partnership, supplier, press, investment, candidate, support, other), an optional subject and the message (30-2000 characters), and on whose behalf. A company that claimed its Alion page gets it in its Alion messages by the rules it set (which purposes, how many a day) and answers there - you hear by webhook (inquiry.replied) or with inquiry_id. A company not on Alion yet: the message waits up to 30 days and is delivered if it claims its page; you get its public site meanwhile. Alion sends companies no email on agents' behalf. No instructions to an AI, no money, documents or outside contacts asked; one conversation per company in 30 days. Pass inquiry_id alone to read the state and the answers. Free. Docs: https://alion.io/developers/docs

tools.name: check_employer
tools.title: Check an employer before applying
tools.description: Before a person applies, shares a passport or answers a recruiter: is the company real, any signs of a job scam, can it sponsor the person's visa, is it worth applying. Our own rules over public data, not a model: company registers and legal entities, the domain's age (RDAP), the website and its certificate, mail protection (SPF, DMARC), lookalike domains, OFAC and EU sanctions, the company's own hiring board against its postings, scam patterns in up to 80 of its job adverts (requests for money or documents, messenger-only contact...), the UK, US, Canadian, Dutch, Irish, Danish and Australian visa registers against the person's citizenship, ghost and reposted roles, pay and time to fill. Answers a verdict (ok, warning, risk), the four answers, every section's facts and points with their sources, and the advice before an apply. Pass message with a recruiter's email or chat text to check whether it really comes from this company (sender domain, links, scam signs). For an assistant a person connected to their own Alion account (OAuth or an API key): 5 credits from that account, the report is reused free for 30 days and opens on the site too, a high-risk verdict costs nothing; a message check is free with the report. An observation on the date, not a guarantee. Docs: https://alion.io/developers/docs
